plan.concept: How the RANSAC algorithm robustly fits a model by identifying and ignoring outlier data points that would otherwise skew standard estimation methods.
learningObjectives: Understand the distinction between inliers (points matching the true model) and outliers (noisy or incorrect data points).
Explain why standard least-squares estimation fails in the presence of even a few extreme outliers.
Describe how RANSAC uses consensus to find the true underlying trend despite significant noise.
plan.keyInsight: Standard least-squares fitting is easily dragged off-course by a single bad data point, whereas RANSAC isolates the true pattern by ignoring points that fall outside a strict consensus threshold.

interactions.label: Estimation Method
interactions.effect: Switches the regression line between a standard Least Squares fit (which uses all points) and a robust RANSAC fit (which only uses inliers).
interactions.teaches: The fundamental difference in sensitivity to outliers between standard regression and robust estimation.

interactions.label: Outlier Distance
interactions.effect: Moves the white outlier points vertically further away from the main trend line.
interactions.teaches: How the leverage of outlier points increases with their distance, drastically pulling standard fits away from the true trend while leaving RANSAC unaffected.

demo_steps.title: Establish the Clean Trend
demo_steps.narration: First, look at the main diagonal cluster of blue points. When outlier distance is set to zero, all points align perfectly, and any standard fitting method can easily identify the correct linear relationship.
demo_steps.focus: The alignment of both the blue inlier points and the white outlier points along a single, clear diagonal trend.

demo_steps.title: The Pull of Outliers
demo_steps.narration: Now, increase the outlier distance. Notice how the red Least Squares line gets dragged downward, tilting away from the blue points. Because least-squares minimizes *all* squared distances, a few far-away points exert immense leverage and ruin the fit.
demo_steps.focus: The tilting red line and the gap growing between the line and the majority of blue inlier points.

demo_steps.title: Robust Fit with RANSAC
demo_steps.narration: Switch the method to RANSAC. Notice how the red line instantly snaps back to perfectly align with the blue points, completely ignoring the white outliers. RANSAC does this by searching for a consensus set of points that fit within a threshold, treating the distant points as noise.
demo_steps.focus: The red line aligning perfectly with the blue circles, while the white circles are visibly disregarded.

plan.reconstructionNotes: An interactive 2D scatter plot with x and y axes. A set of ~10 blue filled circles forms a clear positive linear trend. A set of 2-3 white circles with black borders represents outliers situated to the far right, below the linear trend. A red line representing the fitted model is drawn across the plot. When 'Least Squares' is selected, the line is calculated using standard linear regression on all points. When 'RANSAC' is selected, the line is calculated using only the blue points (inliers).
